english.title: Breach safeguards relating to examination of data - bulk acquisition warrant - Part 6 Investigatory Powers Act 2016
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) deliberately selected communications data, namely **(..SPECIFY DATA..), obtained under a bulk acquisition warrant for examination, knowing or believing that the selection of that data did not comply with a requirement imposed by section 172 in that **(..SPECIFY NON-COMPLIANCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 173(1) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
deliberately selects communications data obtained under a bulk acquisition warrant for examination
knowing or believing that the selection of that data does not comply with a requirement imposed by section 172

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent from the Director of Public Prosecutions is required.
(ii) See section 172 for the safeguards relating to the examination of data obtained under a bulk acquisition warrant.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
INDICTMENT: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.Time limit for prosecutions:
None
